### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via TranslationConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const), defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_

- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), sourceLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os lint (command, 46 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4cf03572859020b10d7df25214a1f08514685370` — the merge of head `34ec0e4f9c46dec9537c4a5525870753f7d4b24d` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4cf03572859020b10d7df25214a1f08514685370 && git checkout 4cf03572859020b10d7df25214a1f08514685370
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 34ec0e4f9c46dec9537c4a5525870753f7d4b24d && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff 34ec0e4f9c46dec9537c4a5525870753f7d4b24d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `34ec0e4f9c46dec9537c4a5525870753f7d4b24d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-bundle-extract.ts

Read for this record: card #33232 (body, triage 6874060759, claim 6878868326, relayed os-dev-report 6881427009), PR #33357 (body, 14-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read on `origin/main` only to judge the scope files. No ruling and no earlier contract-review record exists on the card or the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`TranslationConfigSchema` accept set: widened, right.** `sourceLocale` is a new optional `LocaleSchema` key on a `strictObject`. Before this head, `i18n: { sourceLocale: ... }` was refused as an unknown key, so every stack that parses on `main` parses to the same output here. No existing valid stack changes meaning.
- **Three near-miss keys (`sourceLanguage`, `authoringLocale`, `authoringLanguage`): still refused, right.** They were refused before with the generic unknown-key answer and are refused now with `sourceLocale` as the suggestion. The accept set does not move; only the message does.
- **Public type surface: widened, right.** `TranslationConfig` (a `z.input`) gains one optional property. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` gains exactly `system/TranslationConfig:sourceLocale`, and the regenerated reference row matches the `.describe()` string word for word.
- **`@objectstack/cli` exported surface: unchanged, right.** `resolveSourceLocale` is exported from `utils/i18n-coverage.ts`, which the package's `exports` map (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `./package.json`) does not address.
- **CLI behaviour for stacks without the key: unchanged, right.** `resolveSourceLocale` returns `defaultLocale`, else `en`, which is the expression it replaces in both `computeI18nCoverage` and `extract.ts`. The flag still precedes it at all three call sites.
- **Gated locale set when the key IS declared: narrowed in one shape, wrong as documented.** See ④ finding 1.
- **Gate verdicts:** every check-run on the head concluded success or skipped. That includes Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Test Core 1 to 8, and both type-check families. No check failed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — correct. The PR body and the changeset both carry the line, and the diff widens a published schema's accept set and its exported input type.

`@objectstack/spec: minor` and `@objectstack/cli: minor` match what the diff publishes: one new optional authorable key, and a new CLI reading that only a stack declaring the key can reach. Nothing is removed or narrowed for existing input, so major is not owed. A patch would understate a new authorable key. Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation, refused GitHub writes:** process only. The seat opened the draft PR from the pushed branch and relayed the report verbatim; the tree reviewed here is the pushed head.
- **Dev deviation, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` surface breach:** accepted. The old row ("Defaults to the config's `i18n.defaultLocale`") is false against `resolveSourceLocale`; the new row states the order the code implements.
- **Dev deviation, gate rerun narrowed to 56 commands for the last commit:** moot. The check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts and all are green.
- **Dev deviation, Clause-② measured on the built declarations:** agrees with ① and ②.
- **Open question 1 (should the serving layer read `sourceLocale`): answered A, and escalated.** The schema jsdoc, the docs page and the changeset all publish "not yet read by the serving layer". That is true on `main`: `metaTranslateOptions` passes `getDefaultLocale()` as `ResolveOptions.defaultLocale`, and `serve.ts` collapses the fallback to `fallbackLocale`, else `defaultLocale`. The follow-up card the PR body promises is not filed: an issue search for `sourceLocale` returns only #33232. It is owed before this lands, because until it exists "not yet" points at nothing. It also carries a consequence the PR creates: with the key declared and no `fallbackLocale`, the gate reports the source locale 100% covered while an `en` request is served the `zh-CN` row.
- **Open question 2 (`os i18n check --json` keeps `defaultLocale` for the resolved source locale): answered A.** The `CoverageReport` doc comment states it and the output is unchanged for stacks without the key.
- **Out-of-scope finding, skills docs:** `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` follow-up is declared on the `Skills-docs:` line but not filed. It is owed to the skills lane.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is owed. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — judged against card #33232 (no ruling, no ADR cited) and its first consumer, `computeI18nCoverage`.

The design holds for the card's scenario. One key carried two facts; the new key separates them, defaults to today's reading, uses the same `LocaleSchema`, and carries no `supportedLocales` membership rule, as `defaultLocale` carries none. In the downstream shape (`defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, `sourceLocale: 'en'`, `zh-CN` in `supportedLocales`) the consumer gives zero `en` findings and reports the `zh-CN` gap. The serving-layer caveat is stated in the jsdoc and is true.

1. **should-fix — the jsdoc sentence "they do gate every other declared locale, `defaultLocale` included" is false for a shape the same jsdoc permits.**
   - In `computeI18nCoverage` the gated set is the source locale, plus `supportedLocales`, plus the locales some bundle exists for. The users' `defaultLocale` is never added.
   - On `main` it was always in the set, because it was the source.
   - So `{ defaultLocale: 'zh-CN', sourceLocale: 'en', supportedLocales: ['en', 'es-ES'] }` with no `zh-CN` bundle yet, or the same with `supportedLocales: []`, gates `en` and `es-ES` and reports nothing for `zh-CN`. That is the language every user without a preference is served, and the card's own failure ("loses its zh-CN coverage check") in a narrower shape.
   - `extract.ts` has the same root: `zh-CN` is no longer scaffolded there, though its `--locales` help still says the default locale is always included.
   - Fix either side: add the declared `defaultLocale` to the active set in the three non-override arms (and to the extract locale list), with a test for the shape; or narrow the sentence to "every locale in `supportedLocales`". The first is what the card asks for.

2. **nit — the `.describe()` string omits the serving caveat the jsdoc carries.** The generated reference row and any schema-driven tooltip show only the `.describe()` text, so a reader there is not told the runtime does not read the key. Fixing it regenerates the reference and moves the head; take it with finding 1's fix or leave it to the open-question-1 card.

**Implementing files**

- `i18n-coverage.ts`: `resolveSourceLocale` agrees with the contract sentence by sentence (`sourceLocale`, else `defaultLocale`, else `en`; empty strings skipped; non-object input tolerated). The override precedes it. The `CoverageReport.defaultLocale` and `CoverageOptions.defaultLocale` comments describe what the code does. Finding 1 lives in the unchanged `activeLocales` block below it.
- `extract.ts`: the same single reading, flag first; the comment matches. Finding 1's extract half applies.
- `i18n-bundle-extract.ts`: comment only, and accurate. The source locale is rewritten from the inline text on every merge, as the changeset says.
- `check.ts`, `lint.ts`: the three `--default-locale` help strings state the implemented order.
- **nit** — unchanged neighbours in `check.ts` and `lint.ts` still say "non-default locales" where the code now means non-source: the `--strict` help at `check.ts:114`, the `--i18n-strict` help at `lint.ts:937`, and the closing message at `check.ts:261`. With the key declared, strict mode does raise the users' default locale to an error, which those words exclude. Follow-up or accepted deviation.

Break attempts that held:
- Key absent: the report is identical to the pre-change reading.
- Key equal to `defaultLocale`: identical.
- Key outside `supportedLocales`: the source is added to the gated set and satisfied by inline text.
- `--default-locale` set: it wins.
- Stack composition: `i18n` is a `single` key in `COMPOSE_KEY_DISPOSITIONS`, so the new key is not dropped or merged.

**VERDICT: PASS**
